title: Proposed US tariffs on 'excess industrial capacity'
what_happened: On 2026-11-25 the US Trade Representative found that 14 economies run structural excess industrial capacity and proposed tariffs on them, with ceilings from 15% to 35%. For China the proposal is up to 20%, with an alternative of up to 40% on all goods. Comments close on 2027-01-05 and no effective date is set.
how_it_reaches_markets: Higher import costs feed inflation while rates are already expected to rise; retaliation risk for US exporters; direct hit to Asian and European equity markets.

sourced_facts.text: 2026-11-25: USTR determined that structural excess capacity practices of 14 economies (China, EU, Singapore, Switzerland, Indonesia, Malaysia, Cambodia, Thailand, Korea, Vietnam, Taiwan, Bangladesh, Japan, India) are actionable under Section 301 and proposed to consider tariffs

Proposed ceilings include: Vietnam up to 35%, India up to 25%, China and Singapore up to 20%, five Southeast and South Asian economies up to 18%, EU 15%, Japan, Korea, Switzerland and Taiwan up to 15%
The notice for China adds an alternative of 'a tariff of up to 40 percent' on all goods of China if engagement is inadequate
Written comments are due 2027-01-05 and hearings begin 2027-01-25; no effective date is stated

resolved_when_all: Final rates and effective dates are published, AND either the measures are withdrawn or agreements are announced with China and the EU covering them
worsened_when_any: Tariffs take effect at or above the proposed rates
A named trading partner announces retaliation

relief_headlines_that_do_not_resolve_it: Reports of talks or delays without a published change to the proposed rates
